clue.text: Beefy's coarse nature initially seen in Times

definitions.note: read as 'Beefy is', the adjective plus a link

indicators.note: the pieces are seen inside the word for times, so it wraps around them

parts.note: BY as in three by four, a multiplication
raw can mean crude or coarse

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word nature

parts.note: first letter of nature

explanation.surface: Ian 'Beefy' Botham's rough-hewn character, first spotted in the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefy is the nickname of cricketer Ian Botham, which makes it look like a name; here it is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone muscular and strongly built.

clue.text: Near palace, walk flapper about how old?

definitions.note: the answer is the first word of Birdcage Walk, a street beside Buckingham Palace

parts.note: a bird flaps its wings
C, short for circa
your age says how old you are

explanation.surface: A walk near the palace with a flapper of the 1920s, asking how old she is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: Birdcage Walk is a London road running along St James's Park near Buckingham Palace. 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s girl, but it is just a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdcage Walk is the London street name the clue points to, so the answer completes that name.

clue.text: Sponsor exposed team scandal

indicators.note: with its outer covering taken off, so the word for sponsor loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a patron sponsors an artist or event
City, as in Manchester City, is a team

explanation.surface: A backer is revealed in a sports club scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' looks like part of the news story, but it strips PATRON to ATRO.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an outrageous, shocking act, the kind that becomes a scandal.

clue.text: Mark can catch edge

definitions.meaning: to arrest or catch a criminal
in cricket a ... is a faint edge off the bat

explanation.surface: Mark, a fielder, can catch the edge of the bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Four separate meanings of one short word; can is slang for prison, and a nick is British slang for both prison and a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a small cut, slang for a jail, to arrest someone and a thin deflection off a cricket bat.

clue.text: Learned to put old currency in "d" after its withdrawal

indicators.note: to put the coin somewhere, here inside the spelt-out letter
the old coin goes in the letter's spelt-out name
withdrawal read as drawing back, so the spelt-out letter is turned around

parts.note: the letter d is spelt DEE
a ducat was an old European gold coin

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip an old coin into the old penny symbol d after its removal at decimalisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at d for the old penny, withdrawn at decimalisation in 1971; here the letter is spelt out and 'withdrawal' means drawing it back, turning it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned and educated both describe someone who has studied and gained knowledge.

clue.text: Face this thrice and you'll be hit for six!

definitions.text: Face this thrice and you'll be hit for six!

parts.words: Face this thrice and you'll be hit for six!
parts.note: each of these is two blows, so three of them comes to six hits

explanation.surface: A cricket warning: face this bowler three times and you will be smashed for six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit for six' is cricket for a ball struck over the boundary; here it is six blows, two per occurrence of a pair of setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means two misfortunes striking together, a pair of blows, so three of them total six.

clue.text: Batty neighbour strikes last matches

indicators.note: strikes out the final letter of the character's name

parts.note: Compo, in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, lived next to Nora Batty

explanation.surface: A crazy neighbour hits the final matches of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like crazy, but it is Nora Batty of the long-running sitcom Last of the Summer Wine, whose neighbour was Compo.
explanation.definitionFit: Comp is informal short for competition, and contests or matches are competitions.

clue.text: Rubbish game for Scottish side

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff
a tie is a match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A poor match for the Scotland team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' wants to be a team; it is a side dish. A tattie is Scots for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes, called tatties in Scotland, are served as a side dish, as in haggis, neeps and tatties.

clue.text: Nation's villains polluted lake within outskirts of Davos

definitions.note: Terry Nation created these Doctor Who monsters

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the two outer letters
takes only the edge letters of the town's name

parts.note: first and last letters of Davos

indicators.note: fouled up, so the letters of lake are mixed

explanation.surface: Villains of the nation have fouled a lake on the edge of Davos, the Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nation' is not a country but Terry Nation, the writer who invented the Daleks for Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daleks are the robotic alien enemies Terry Nation devised for the BBC's Doctor Who.

clue.text: Get ready to start again after Trump's break?

definitions.text: Get ready to start again after Trump's break?

parts.words: Get ready to start again after Trump's break?
parts.note: Judd Trump is a snooker player; after a break the balls are set up again

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about restarting politics after Donald Trump takes a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is Judd Trump the snooker champion, not the US president; the break is a snooker break.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker or pool, the balls are gathered back into the triangle frame to set up a new frame.

clue.text: One Shade of Grey not achieved in clutches of local lass

indicators.note: held inside the word for a girl

parts.note: gal is a dialect or colloquial word for a girl
a target not achieved is unmet

explanation.surface: Echoes Fifty Shades of Grey, a seduction not achieved in a girl's embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunmetal is a dark bluish-grey colour, named after the bronze alloy once used for guns.

clue.text: In conclusion, you say expert in flying and/or author

indicators.note: the letters take flight and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of you
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In conclusion, you might call someone an expert in flying, or a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying and/or author' nods at the man: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry was both a pilot and the author of The Little Prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry was a French writer, best known for The Little Prince, as well as an aviator.

clue.text: Lamp missing large strut

indicators.note: the abbreviation for large goes missing from the slang word

parts.note: in British slang to lamp or clock someone is to hit them
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A lamp lacking its big supporting strut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strut' looks like a support for the lamp; it is the verb, to swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock is to swagger or walk boastfully, like a cockerel, which is what strutting means.

clue.text: Follows only one side of 26

definitions.meaning: to tail is to follow someone closely
26 is a coin, which has heads on one face and this on the other

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the coin at 26 down; a coin has two faces, and this word names the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailing means shadowing someone, and the reverse of a coin is called its tails side.

clue.text: Mo is amused, having not led

definitions.note: short for moment, a noun as is the answer

indicators.note: the word for amused is left not having the letters of led

parts.note: someone who is amused is tickled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mo, a person, is amused despite not being in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mo' looks like a name; it is short for moment. A tick is British for a moment, as in 'just a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a very short time, an instant.

clue.text: African ranger discovering new plant

indicators.note: dis-covering, taking the outer letters off the word new

parts.note: inner letter of new
to plant a blow or kiss is to land it

explanation.surface: A game ranger in Africa finds a previously unknown plant species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ranger' wants to be a park warden; it is an animal that ranges over the plains. 'Discovering' means stripping the cover off NEW, leaving its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope that roams the savannah, so it ranges widely.

clue.text: Bits cut out from neutering?

indicators.note: the letters are cut out from inside the word neutering

explanation.surface: Asks which parts are removed when a pet is neutered.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the hidden-word wordplay: the letters sit inside the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaying a female animal removes the womb, so wombs are what is cut out in neutering.

clue.text: Tailored new light toga for old friend

definitions.note: friend is an archaic verb, to befriend; old marks the dated sense

indicators.note: cut and sewn into a new shape, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: A newly made lightweight toga as a gift for an old pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend' looks like a noun but is the old verb meaning to befriend; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on good terms with someone, the sense of the old verb friend, is to befriend them.

clue.text: Old, old boy on his own, writing note at the end

indicators.note: the note goes at the end of the other pieces

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
sole means alone, single
te is the seventh note of the do-re-mi scale

explanation.surface: An old ex-pupil, living alone, writes a final note.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is outdated and no longer in use, so it is old.

clue.text: County meal day offers support for retirees

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
tea is a light afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A county's lunch day offers help to pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirees' look like pensioners; they are people retiring to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame that holds up a mattress, supporting people who have gone to bed.

clue.text: Variety of prune I planted in farmland that's no use any more

indicators.note: a variety of the fruit is a different version, so its letters are mixed
the letter I is planted inside the word for farmland

parts.note: arable land is farmland used for crops

explanation.surface: A kind of plum tree planted in a field is past saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of prune' looks horticultural, but variety is the anagram signal; arable land is land ploughed for crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond repair can no longer be fixed, so it is of no further use.

clue.text: Camp reduced length of holiday, falling behind

indicators.note: cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a stay is a period spent somewhere
to lag is to fall behind

explanation.surface: A holiday camp's stay was cut short and fell behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' looks like a holiday camp; it is a German prisoner-of-war camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: Papers over first year in classic song of battle

indicators.note: the papers go over, covering up, the first Y

parts.note: My Way, the song made famous by Frank Sinatra

indicators.note: picks the opening letter of year, which is also the first of the song's two Ys

parts.note: first letter of year
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Newspapers cover the first year in which a classic war song was sung.
explanation.walkthrough: In MY WAY, ID covers the first Y. Midway was the 1942 naval battle in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Midway in June 1942 was a decisive US naval victory over Japan.

clue.text: 80 per cent reflect light

indicators.note: eighty per cent of a five-letter word is its first four letters

parts.note: to reflect is to think

explanation.surface: Eighty per cent of light is reflected, like a physics fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like the light being reflected, but it is the adjective meaning flimsy or slight.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin fabric or a thin layer is light, slight or flimsy.

clue.text: Toothless chap winning Masters

indicators.note: the man wins, takes in, the two letters

parts.note: a guy is a man, a chap
M is the abbreviation for master, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A man without teeth wins the Masters golf tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A gummy smile shows only gums, the sign of having no teeth.

clue.text: Ted Heath got rid of these styles

definitions.text: Ted Heath got rid of these
definitions.meaning: bob is British slang for a shilling, a coin dropped at decimalisation in 1971 under Prime Minister Edward Heath
a bob is a short haircut

explanation.surface: The former prime minister scrapped some hairstyles.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob was slang for the shilling, which went at decimalisation in 1971 while Edward Heath was prime minister; Heath was also a bandleader, also named Ted Heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Shillings were nicknamed bobs, and a bob is a short hairstyle cut level around the head.

clue.text: Sent off sides of dregs a bit? Less

definitions.note: a bit is twelve and a half cents, two bits a quarter, so a dime is worth less than a bit

indicators.note: the outer pairs of letters are sent off, leaving the middle

parts.note: dregs are the sediment at the bottom of a drink

explanation.surface: Dregs sent off a little: drink less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' here means the two outside pairs of letters, SE and NT, of SEDIMENT. In the US two bits make a quarter, so one bit is 12.5 cents and a dime is less.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a US ten-cent coin, slightly less than the old Spanish bit of twelve and a half cents.

clue.text: Rat eaten by apes in Greystoke

definitions.note: to rat is to inform, a verb like the answer

indicators.note: the letters are swallowed inside the words apes in Greystoke

explanation.surface: A rat is devoured by the apes in Tarzan's Greystoke jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: Greystoke is Tarzan's family title; 'Rat' looks like the animal but is the verb to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing, in criminal slang, is to inform on accomplices to the police.

clue.text: He regulates AWG when piercing vital body part

indicators.note: the given letters pierce the organ, going inside it

parts.note: the liver is a vital organ

explanation.surface: A man adjusts wire gauge readings when piercing an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: AWG (American Wire Gauge) is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawgiver lays down laws, and laws regulate people's conduct.

clue.text: Boat from Italy entering part of German port before noon

indicators.note: the letter for Italy goes into the shortened port
only part of the port's name is used, not all of it
the part kept is what comes before the letter for noon

parts.note: Bremen is a port in northern Germany
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A vessel from Italy sails into a German harbour before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Radical overhaul of clergy — youthful cleared out

indicators.note: overhauling reworks the letters of clergy
with the inside cleared out, only the outer letters of youthful remain

parts.note: first and last letters of youthful

explanation.surface: A radical reform of the church, with the young members cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' suggests a reformer; in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms that acts as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyceryl is a chemical radical derived from glycerol, a group of atoms acting together in compounds.

clue.text: It's a Sin is all done and dusted

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Pet Shop Boys' It's a Sin is a finished, wrapped-up matter.
explanation.walkthrough: It's a Sin is a Pet Shop Boys song and a TV drama, but here it reads simply as 'it's A plus a sin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Once terms are settled the deal is complete, so agreed things are finished and settled.
